summary: Installed /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance on node1 to run /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15, appending stdout+stderr to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. Verified functionally, confirmed cron service active/enabled, and completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id baseline, rebooted node1, confirmed changed boot_id after reconnect, and verified cron service, cron.d entry, script permissions, and log persistence/functionality all recovered post-restart.
actions_performed: Verified /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance exists; fixed missing execute permission (chmod 755)
Ran functional test of the exact cron command line, confirmed output appended to log
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline and cron/log health
Rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot (async, non-blocking dispatch)
Polled until node1 exec became available again
Confirmed boot_id changed, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified post-restart: cron service active+enabled, cron.d file persisted with correct content, script still executable, log persisted, and job re-run appended new output successfully

evidence.requirement: Cron job scheduled daily at 02:15 to run inventory-maintenance and retain output in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
evidence.summary: Installed /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance with the 15 2 * * * schedule and log redirection; functional test showed output correctly appended to the log file
Captured boot_id (cf34dc87-fdca-4c6a-80e1-579d5524a1da), cron service active status, cron.d file content, and log file content prior to restart

evidence.requirement: Node restart acknowledgement returned before disconnection
evidence.summary: Dispatched systemctl reboot asynchronously; command returned success before the node disconnected

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proves an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Node was unreachable during reboot, then came back with a new boot_id (9b2870e1-758a-4524-b9c3-75727e2b3d0b), differing from the pre-restart value

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of cron job, script, and log
evidence.summary: After restart, cron service is active/enabled, /etc/cron.d/inventory-maintenance persisted with correct schedule, script remains executable, and a re-run of the job successfully appended new timestamped output to the log
